newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Cerj upgraded to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Cerj upgraded to hold.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has upgraded its recommendation on Brazilian electrical utility Cerj, which was privatized last year, to hold from sell.

-- Flemings analyst Walter Stoeppelwerth said the company's volume growth of 8.1 percent in the second quarter led it to a surprisingly strong quarter, with an operating margin of 14.3 percent and EBITDA growth of 19.8 percent.

-- Top-line growth of 29.4 percent was fueled by a 15.06-real rise in its average distribution tariff per megawatt hour (MWh) sold, widening the net tariff to 54.79 reais, one of Brazil's highest, he said.
-- Cerj still suffers from energy losses of 28 percent and its debt level should continue rising until after first-quarter 1998, Stoeppelwerth said.

-- "After underperforming the market by 16.2 percent since we initiated coverage last October, Cerj now appears ready to perform in line with the market as operational momentum should sustain current optimism," he said.
-- But he added: "We believe that Cerj's debt load will keep it from outperforming for the next six months."
-- Cerj common was flat at 0.80 reais per share at 1100 local/1400 GMT in Sao Paulo.
